# HF: Claims Trends You Need to Know in 2026

Industry News

16th February 2026

![](https://mgaa.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/HF-Navy-NO-TEXT-Logo-300x300.png)

### AI

HF sees 2026 as a pivotal year in the implementation of AI into insurance processes, including claims handling. Some key developments our experts are monitoring are the use of predictive analytics to spot and manage claims trends and enable data-driven decision making, process automation and implementing agentic AI which can take initiative, carry out multi-stage projects and act with greater autonomy. The key to success will be balancing technological efficiencies with the need for human management and input where necessary.

### Claims Inflation

CPI inflation in the UK was at 3.4% in December 2025, however the Bank of England predicts a downward trajectory, to around 2.2% in by Q4 2026. This could help the upwards trend of claims inflation, but HF’s litigation teams are seeing other key drivers continue, such as global supply chain disruption (see below), labour shortages driving up service costs and the costs of repairs and remedial works increasing. Overall, claims inflation is expected to continue in 2026.

### Consumer Duty

Since the consumer duty came into force in 2023, the FCA has increased the level and scope of its oversight into insurers’ compliance. This is expected to continue, meaning that insurers will have to pay greater heed to FCA reviews and ensure they are proactively implementing the required improvements in claims management and customer experience. The FCA was initially concentrating on education, but now HF expects that enforcement action will increase against firms who fail to meet their duties.

### Cyber Threats

The major incidents M&S and John Lewis experienced in 2025 shone a light on cyber losses often extending far beyond incident response and IT recovery. It is now evident that business interruption and operational disruption can quickly become the dominant losses, particularly where online activity, logistics, manufacturing or supplier connectivity are impacted. HF’s Cyber Team is seeing a clearer pipeline of downstream legal exposure, in the form of customer and employee data claims, contractual disputes with suppliers and service providers, and litigation asserting inadequate controls or governance.

### ESG

_Environment_ – Climate change is fueling more frequent severe weather events which cause a cascade of claims as well as disrupting manufacturing and causing shortages of raw materials which impacts the global supply chain. All of this drives up claims inflation. With global warming on an upwards trajectory, we expect this trend to continue within the UK and globally. Insurers may also see decreasing returns on any investment portfolios which focus on fossil fuels or carbon-heavy industries, impacting bottom lines.

_Social_ – With increasing awareness and cultural expectations in respect of diversity, equity and inclusion, our Casualty Team is seeing more claims relating to discrimination and failure to implement reasonable adjustments. Likewise, EL claims continue to be prevalent as people seek to enforce higher and higher standards of welfare, health and safety at work.

_Governance_ – 2026 sees two big regulatory exercises which will place an operational strain on many insurers. Firstly, the PRA’s Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test (DyGIST) in May 2026; an exercise to test solvency and liquidity resilience and risk management actions of selected insurers. Secondly, many insurers must provide a Solvent Exit Analysis to the PRA by June 2026. Although these exercises will no doubt divert resources in the short term, they offer an opportunity to review claims management (and other) processes and implement best practice solutions going forward.

### Fraud

Over recent years, HF’s Fraud Team has noted that the landscape has moved away from opportunistic individuals to more sophisticated enterprises. The focus of counter-fraud efforts is now on professional enablers, such as mechanics inflating repair bills or medical experts adding fictitious or exaggerated injuries to reports. Going forward, there will be an even greater need for enhanced data sharing between insurers and their professional advisors to identify rogue behaviour, and there may be increasing pressure to improve the sanctions available to regulators and law enforcement to tackle professional fraud set-ups.

### Geopolitical Landscape

The geopolitical landscape continues to be volatile including the wars in Ukraine and Gaza and Trump’s unpredictable presidency which has resulted in the US threatening to take control of nation states and widening economic sanctions on imports into the US. This instability has a knock-on effect on global trade and supply chains, which ultimately increases the costs and lifecycle of claims. Unfortunately, our litigation experts see little prospect of any marked improvement any time soon.

### Proactive Risk Management

In HF’s experience, insurers are focussing more than ever on proactive risk management. Where insurers, brokers, insureds and professional advisors invest in partnerships aimed at mapping and reducing risks, this can have a significant effect on claims volumes and values. With AI and data-analytics improving year on year, shared learning and greater involvement in claims handling and risk management process will pay-off dividends for those willing to invest in a collaborative process.
